title: When the Inheritance Turns
premise: True-crime podcaster Kestrel Montrose has spent years quietly solving deaths the police wrote off as accidents, so when a drowned stranger washes up at Gullwrack Cove wearing clothes stolen from Kestrel's own closet, the message is unmistakable: someone knows what they know. Following a shipping ledger hidden in the victim's antique shop inventory, Kestrel uncovers a decades-old smuggling ring whose surviving members have been erasing witnesses one 'accident' at a time — including the drowning of Kestrel's mother, the case that started it all. As the tide gives up its dead and the killer closes in, Kestrel must choose between handing the evidence to a compromised police force and delivering justice themselves. In the end, Kestrel broadcasts the confession on air, forcing the town to reckon with its buried past while accepting that survival cost them the last person they trusted.
about_author: Lior Villalobos grew up in a coastal fishing town where every family kept one story they never told, an inheritance of silence that shaped their obsession with unsolved deaths. A former court stenographer turned novelist, they write mysteries about people who take justice into their own hands because the law arrived too late.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps Receipts
chapters.summary: Kestrel Montrose records the final episode of their cold-case season in the attic studio above Gullwrack Cove, reflecting on three accidents they quietly proved were murders. A knock at dawn: a body on the shingle, dressed in Kestrel's missing clothes. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in vindication — the work has finally found them.

chapters.title: A Stranger Wearing My Winter Coat
chapters.summary: Detective Imogen Sarkis, once a source Kestrel burned, arrives to investigate and immediately suspects them. The victim is identified as Edmund Voss, an antiquarian who recently bought a crate of ledgers from a shuttered estate. POV: alternating Kestrel and Sarkis. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion sharpening into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: In Voss's shop, Kestrel recognizes the accounting format from their mother's old bookkeeping job — double columns concealing a second set of numbers written in tide-table ciphers. The ledger maps forty years of smuggled cargo and payments to town officials. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling as familiar names surface.

chapters.title: Everyone in Town Owes Someone
chapters.summary: Kestrel interviews aging townsfolk for the podcast, using episodes as cover for interrogation. A retired harbormaster hints that Voss was asking about a 1987 drowning before he died. That night, Kestrel's studio is ransacked — but nothing taken except the ledger's cipher key page. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: What My Mother Was Doing in 1987
chapters.summary: Digging through family boxes, Kestrel finds their mother's matching half of the ledger and realizes she wasn't just a bookkeeper — she was the ring's accountant, and her drowning was the price of trying to leave. POV: Kestrel, with flashback interludes. Emotional beat: grief recontextualized; the case was always personal.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: The harbormaster is found dead in his boat, ruled another accident, hours after agreeing to go on record. Sarkis admits the investigation is being steered from above and secretly gives Kestrel the coroner's file. POV: Sarkis. Emotional beat: her crisis of loyalty — the badge or the truth.

chapters.title: Three Survivors, One Secret
chapters.summary: The ledger's final pages name three living partners: the town's beloved matriarch, the current harbormaster, and Kestrel's estranged uncle Aldous. Confronting Aldous, Kestrel learns he's been paying protection money for decades to keep Kestrel alive. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with unexpected love.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: The matriarch lures Kestrel to the cove with a false confession, intending to make them the fourth accident. Kestrel escapes by triggering the emergency beacon hidden in their podcast equipment, but loses the original ledger to the incoming tide. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: terror, then cold clarity — they no longer need the paper.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Kestrel goes live with a finale episode: the decoded ledger, the coroner's files, and a recorded call in which the matriarch all but confesses. The town listens in real time; Sarkis makes arrests on air despite orders to stand down. POV: alternating Kestrel and Sarkis. Emotional beat: catharsis — justice delivered outside the law, through the law's own microphone.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returned
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the tide deposits the waterlogged ledger on the same shingle where Voss washed ashore. Kestrel buries their mother's half beside the cove, ends the podcast, and begins writing this book instead. Aldous visits; forgiveness remains unfinished. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: hard-won peace — survival's price paid, memory finally given a grave.
